Investors previously sold $CRDO over copper decline fears, but players like $MXL and $ALAB are now entering due to a 49% CAGR through 2030. Credo retains an estimated 90% AEC market share and is the most trusted vendor with relationships to 5/6 major hyperscalers including $SPCX. text:
$CRDO is down today because $MXL is planning to compete with them in the 1.6T AEC market.

What I think is funny is investors sold off $CRDO on their last earnings out of fear copper was a declining market. Now how we have players like $MXL and $ALAB moving in on it, because in reality it has a 49% CAGR through 2030.

Credo still has an estimated 90% share of the AEC market and is by far the most trusted vendor, especially considering it has relationships with 5/6 major hyperscalers including $SPCX which has the most aggressive GW roadmap over the next 18 months. 

What's interesting as well for $CRDO is 1/3 of their business could be optical networking by 2028, so a lot of their growth is coming from a completely different market that's growing even faster.

$CRDO is starting to look ridiculously cheap.

zh_summary: @SawyerMerritt：美國國家公路交通安全管理局提出新規，移除無方向盤及踏板自動駕駛車輛（如Tesla Cybercab）的聯邦監管障礙，包括取消手動轉向燈控制要求。
en_summary: @SawyerMerritt: NHTSA proposed rules to remove federal barriers for autonomous vehicles without steering wheels or pedals, such as Tesla's Cybercab, including dropping manual turn signal control requirements.
text:
NHTSA announced today that they are proposing new rules aimed at removing U.S. federal regulatory barriers for autonomous vehicles without steering wheels or pedals, such as @Tesla's Cybercab.

The proposed changes include:
• Eliminating requirements for manually operated turn signal controls in vehicles without steering wheels or pedals: "NHTSA has concluded that the self-canceling and manually operated control requirements in the current standard are unnecessary for turn signal operating units that are installed on vehicles without manually operated driving controls."

• Allowing autonomous driving systems to control turn signals, hazard lights, and high/low beams without traditional driver-operated switches.

• Removing certain dashboard indicator requirements for turn signals and high beams in vehicles without manual driving controls.

• Allowing optional cyan-colored exterior lights to indicate when a vehicle is operating autonomously, with standardized requirements for their placement, brightness, and operation.

• Eliminating outdated restrictions on vertical headlight arrangements, giving automakers greater design flexibility.

• Allowing modern integrated headlights to be tested at manufacturer-specified voltages rather than requiring 12.8 volts.

NHTSA says the changes are intended to eliminate unnecessary regulatory barriers, reduce costs, and enable innovation without compromising vehicle safety.

en_summary: @StockSavvyShay: $CRDO controls about 86% of the AEC installed base as AI data centers use its lower cost, power efficient copper cables, and designing its own SerDes chips lets it capture more revenue per connection.
text:
$CRDO now controls ~86% of the AEC installed base as AI data centers rely on its lower-cost, power-efficient copper cables to connect GPUs and switches across large clusters.

That lead becomes super valuable as Credo designs its own SerDes chips and sells complete cables allowing it to capture more revenue from every connection as AI infrastructure scales.

And when a single faulty cable can disrupt thousands of GPUs then hyperscalers have little reason to move away from a supplier already proven at scale which makes Credo's market share incredibly difficult to displace.
